result.summary: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option that rewrites existing block and undo files under a new random or user-specified XOR key before chainstate loading. File rewrites occur sequentially in 1 MiB chunks, using staged files and directory commits to guarantee crash safety and resumability across restarts. Also logs a notice recommending reobfuscation when an unobfuscated blocks directory is detected, and exposes progress through kernel notifications for the GUI and RPC warmup.
result.problem: Nodes synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with an all-zero XOR key (unobfuscated). Node operators currently have no native way to obfuscate existing files, rotate keys, or remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire chain from scratch.
evidence: PR description: "Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing."
Author benchmarks demonstrate migration speeds on an ~850 GB datadir ranging from ~10 minutes on modern SSDs to over 24 hours on an HDD attached to a Raspberry Pi.
result.changed_since_previous: Unchanged in high-level approach; includes minor preparatory cleanups that remove an unused BaseIndex database obfuscation parameter and refine directory commit error reporting.
result.card: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files under a random or user-specified XOR key without resyncing. Nodes synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 have zero-keyed, unobfuscated block files, exposing them to false-positive corruption by antivirus scanners, with no native way to migrate or rotate keys. The migration runs before chainstate loading, stages files with commits to guarantee safe resumption after crashes or interruptions, and reports progress to GUI notifications and logs. Benchmark numbers show migration times of ~10 minutes on NVMe SSD to ~24 hours on HDD for ~850 GB datadirs.

risk.why: A bug in chunk copying, XOR transformation, or directory renaming could corrupt block storage files on disk, requiring an operator to reindex or redownload the chain.
